tools.name: me
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Who this credential belongs to: email, plan, credit balance. Needs the read scope.

tools.name: capabilities_list
tools.title: What Shapeless can do
tools.description: Everything Shapeless can do, live or planned, with the REST routes, MCP tools and CLI lines for each and its page. A planned one says how to get the same outcome today and carries a want door; one with a route answers 501 there until it ships. Needs the read scope (over REST it needs no key).

tools.name: capabilities_want
tools.title: Tell me when it ships
tools.description: Ask to be told the day a planned capability ships. Bound to this account's sign-in email; add an email or https webhookUrl to tell somewhere else. Ask the human first. Needs the read scope.

webhookUrl.description: Optional: an https URL that gets a POST when it ships.

note.description: Optional: what you wanted it for. We read these.

tools.name: tools_list
tools.title: Shapeless tools
tools.description: The live catalog of the Shapeless studio agent's tools, each with its JSON Schema input and default price. Every one is also its own MCP tool here (generate_image, generate_footage, edit_footage, render_carousel, web_search, x_pulse and the rest); this is the read for what the deployment serves right now. Needs the read scope.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.title: Generate an image
tools.description: Make one image from a prompt written as a scene in prose, in the aspect ratio of the platform it is for, optionally conditioned on up to 6 reference_keys from the media library (a logo, a product shot, an earlier image). quality "premium" is the dearer model. Returns the image as a media key with a URL; put the key in posts_create mediaKeys. SPENDS CREDIT: about $0.016 of engine cost a default call, billed with the plan's margin; budgetUsd caps it (default 2, max 10) and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

name.description: A 2-6 word filename for this image, the way you would describe it to a colleague - e.g. "founder desk golden hour". Becomes the file the user sees in their Assets.

prompt.description: The full scene as 2-5 sentences of flowing prose, directing medium, subject, setting, light, and composition — YES "A photorealistic overhead shot of a cluttered founder desk at golden hour, one glowing laptop as the focal point, deep negative space on the right", NOT "desk, laptop, startup, 4k, trending, professional". When reference_keys are given, also say what each referenced object does in the scene.

quality.description: standard = the default model (default). premium = the fidelity escalation, several times the price.

reference_keys.description: Up to 6 media keys to condition on: brand-asset keys from the digest, mediaKeys of earlier generated images, or chat-upload keys. Omit for a purely imagined scene.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: generate_footage
tools.title: Generate AI video
tools.description: Generate one short AI video clip from a prompt: one continuous camera move over one subject, silent unless with_audio (more per second). The dearest asset there is; try find_footage first. The clip carries a SynthID watermark and needs an AI-generated label where the platform asks. Returns a media key. SPENDS CREDIT: about $0.18 of engine cost a default call, billed with the plan's margin; budgetUsd caps it (default 2, max 10) and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

name.description: A 2-6 word filename for this clip, as you would describe it to a colleague - e.g. "rain on window neon". Becomes the file the user sees in their Assets.

prompt.description: The shot as 1-3 sentences of flowing prose: subject, setting, light, and the ONE camera move. Say what the camera does, not what the story means.

duration_seconds.description: 4, 6, 8 (6 by default); anything else rounds up, and you are billed for the rounded length. You pay per second, and you will cut most of it.

aspect.description: Shape of the generated frame. 9:16 by default.

resolution.description: 720p by default and right for b-roll under a cut. 1080p costs $0.05/s against $0.03/s - worth it only when the clip fills the frame and holds.

with_audio.description: Generate the clip's own sound too - $0.05/s at 720p against $0.03/s silent. Default false, because narration, music and sfx normally own the mix and a generated soundtrack fights them. Worth it when the clip sound IS the point: rain, a crowd, a machine, a diegetic moment that carries the shot. An unmuted clip is mixed into the master.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: edit_footage
tools.title: Edit a video
tools.description: Cut a video in the media library (an upload, a generated or found clip, a render) down to the moments that matter and get a new media key: keep beats or quoted words from probe_media's transcript (keep_text), or seconds (keep_ranges, remove_ranges). The same call reframes to 9:16, tightens pauses, burns in captions, lays music and places overlays, a logo and a look. Run probe_media first; plan: true reads the paper edit back before rendering. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

media_key.description: The clip to edit, as a mediaKey from media_library, an upload, or find_footage.

name.description: A 2-6 word filename for the cut, e.g. "demo hero moments". The user sees it in Assets.

keep_text.description: The moments to KEEP, one span per "|", as beats from probe_media's transcript ("b1 | b4-b7 | b12") or as the take's own words ("That's exactly what I did ... make some money | I advise you to check it out"), joined in the order given. A quoted span runs from its first phrase to the end of its last ("..." between them); one phrase alone keeps just those words; it must open and close on a thought or a clause. Quote words as probe_media spells them; a phrase said twice takes #2 ("check it out#2"). The cut lands on the words, with a breath of air either side, never mid-word.

keep_ranges.description: The moments to KEEP, in seconds of the source, joined in the order given: "12.5-18.2, 41-55.5". A timecode ("1:05-1:12") works too. For footage with no speech; a take is cut with keep_text.

remove_ranges.description: The moments to DROP, same format; what remains is joined. Use instead of keep_ranges, never with it.

append_media_keys.description: Other clips joined on AFTER this cut, in the order given, as a comma-separated list of mediaKeys. Each is appended whole - trim it in its own edit first if you only want part of it.

speed.description: Play the cut faster or slower - 1.5 tightens a demo, 0.5 holds a detail. Audio keeps its pitch. 1 (unchanged) by default.

reframe.description: Re-crop to this shape. Leave unset to keep the source framing.

focus.description: "face" finds the person in every kept segment and frames on them, eyes on the upper third - what a talking head wants. Or where the subject is in the SOURCE frame, as "x,y" percentages: "30,50" keeps the left third of a screen recording in a 9:16 crop. Centre by default. Works with or without reframe.

tighten.description: Transcript-first cut: pauses over 0.5s close to 0.3s (0.45s at a sentence end), dead air before the first word and after the last goes, fillers ("um", "uh") are lifted out, and a sentence said twice keeps its last saying (the founder's retake). Every other word stays. The first thing to do to any recorded take.

punch_in.description: Frame every other segment closer, each cut by its own amount (7 to 22%, never the same twice in a row), so each cut reads as a change of shot. With focus "face" the closer framing stays on the person. The jump-cut convention of every talking-head short.

cutout.description: Cutout mode, the shape the best founder reels run in: the speaker is lifted off their background (a real matte, hair and all) and shrunk to a corner, so the product takes the frame while the take keeps playing. Beats, each "<window> anchor [height%]", one per semicolon: "@"paste the URL"..@"analyze" bottom-right; 12-38 bottom-center 45". Anchors: bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right, top-left, top-right, center; the height is a share of the frame, 50 by default. Outside the beats the take is full frame. Put an overlay layer in every beat - a screenshot, a card, the product - or the person is small in front of nothing. A whoosh lands where the mode changes when studio_sound or normalize_audio is on. The reels run three quarters of their length in it: hook and CTA full frame, the demo in cutout.

cutout_backdrop.description: What fills the frame behind the cutout: "blur" (the media overlay on screen, enlarged to cover the frame and blurred, so the product's own colours bleed into the frame; the take itself when no media is on screen; the default) or a hex colour. Needs cutout. For a picture of your own there, use background instead.

background.description: A media key drawn behind the matted speaker in every cutout beat, instead of the blur: a brand backdrop, a product shot, a gradient, or a video that loops (a rendered motion background, a find_footage b-roll). Overlays still sit on top of it. Needs cutout; replaces cutout_backdrop.

sfx.description: Sounds you place, one per line or semicolon: "<window> <sound> [gain dB]", e.g. "@"the result" ding; @"but then" record scratch -3; 12.4 riser". The sound lands as the window opens. Name it by id or by a few words ("vinyl scratch", "whoosh deep"), or media:<mediaKey> for a sound in the library. A placed sound replaces an automatic one within 0.3 s; the automatic pops and whooshes stay everywhere else. Default gain -6 dB. A few per short land; a hit on every sentence is noise. Library ids: air-horn, among-us-role-reveal, anime-wow, applause, apple-pay, bell-ding, boing, bone-crack, bruh, camera-shutter, cash-register, censor-beep, crowd-gasp, deadpan-bruh, ding, discord-notification, drama-boom, dramatic-boomer, dramatic-sting, emotional-damage, error-buzzer, fah, glitch, illuminati-confirmed, keyboard-typing, loading-lag, mac-quack, mario-jump, metal-gear-alert, minecraft-hurt, mouse-click, nelly-ahh, oh-my-god-vine, omg-hell-nah, page-turn, pop, price-is-right-fail, record-scratch, riser, rizz, romance-meme, run-vine, sad-meow, sad-trombone, sad-violin, sanctuary-guardian-what, shocked, shutter-modern, shutter-old, skedaddle, snapchat-notification, spongebob-fail, sub-drop, swoosh-transition, ta-da, triggered, ui-switch, vine-boom, vinyl-scratch, whip, whoosh, whoosh-deep, whoosh-short, wilhelm-scream, windows-xp-error, yippee.

music.description: A bed under the take: "<mediaKey> [gain dB] [duck dB]", e.g. "music/lofi-bed.mp3 -18 12". The voice stays; the bed loops to the cut's length, sits at the gain (-18 by default, under a voice) and is pulled down by the duck amount while the person speaks, back up in the gaps. The key is plan_music's mediaKey or any audio in the library. Masters the cut's sound like normalize_audio.

overlays.description: Pictures ON the cut, on the words or seconds named, one per line or semicolon: "<mediaKey> <window> [full|anchor] [width%]". full fills the frame (the demo_page clip or a screenshot behind a cutout speaker); an anchor (top, top-right, right, bottom-left, ...) places a white card in the safe area, 46% wide by default, popping in. A video key plays, an image is drawn. The window is the words it goes on (@"paste the URL"..@"analyze") or seconds of the CUT, after tighten and the ranges, so the picture lands on the noun. A video holds its last frame once it ends: give a clip a window its length, or a longer clip (demo_page: more steps, or "for 2s" holds); the result names a hold. Never fill a window with a still: end the cutout beat where the clip ends instead.

pops.description: The small things the reels pop beside the speaker ON the word, one per line or semicolon: "<what> <window> [anchor] [size%]". what: brand:nvidia (a company or product's real mark, its own app tile - tiktok, instagram, youtube, linkedin, x, meta, openai, claude, claude-code, gemini, cursor, or any handle brand_mark returned; a domain like jev.ai reaches the long tail), wordmark:claude (the name written the brand's way, on white paper, wider - for a brand the viewer must read, not just recognise), icon:rocket (lucide, a white glyph on a tile in the caption accent), emoji:🔥 or emoji:fire (animated; any other emoji draws as a still), "13,255 visits" (a few words on a dark pill, the last word in the caption accent, quoted), or a media key (a screenshot or logo on a white card). Anchor top by default; in cutout mode the free band is above the speaker, so top, top-left, top-right. One pop per product noun, on the word: @"TikTok". A named platform gets its mark: "TikTok, Reels and Shorts" is three marks in a row (brand:tiktok @"TikTok"..@"Shorts" top-left; brand:instagram @"Reels"..@"Shorts" top; brand:youtube @"Shorts" top-right). The CTA beat shows where to go: the domain in a pill ("shapelessai.com" @"check it out"..end top).

card.description: The hook card: "<4 to 8 words> <window>", e.g. "Get customers for your product 0-5" or "... @"That's exactly"+4". The pops' dark pill in the upper third, popping in, gone when the window closes. The reels pin one from the first half second, with an icon row above the words: add "| brand:meta + <logo mediaKey> = emoji:🚀" (the same whats as pops, a brand in its real colours, joined by + and =), or one mark alone, "| brand:meta", each on its tile, popping in one after the other.

logo.description: The brand lockup small in a corner the whole cut: "<mediaKey> <window> [anchor] [width%] [| Brand Name]" ("0-45" or @"ShapelessAI"..end), top-right and 14% of the frame wide by default, a margin off the edge, the name beside the mark when given (always give it). It fades in and out and steps aside on its own while a full picture, the hook card or a pop on the same corner is on screen. Use the exact logo asset from the brand kit; beside the hook words it goes in the card's icon row.

look.description: Grade the picture, a choice for flat footage or a brand, not a default: clean lifts contrast, colour and sharpness a touch; film is softer with a warm tint and grain; noir is high-contrast black and white; warm is saturated and sunny. Unset keeps the camera's colour, which is right for most phone footage.

studio_sound.description: Studio sound for a recorded voice: rumble and room noise out, mud cut, presence lifted, sibilance tamed, then levelled to feed loudness. Use it on any take a person recorded; not on music or a produced mix.

fit.description: cover (default) crops to fill the new shape; contain letterboxes onto pad_color, which keeps a whole slide readable. Needs reframe.

pad_color.description: The letterbox colour behind a 'contain' reframe, as hex. Default #000000. Match it to the clip or the brand - black bars on a light screen recording read as a broken export. Needs reframe.

captions.description: Word-by-word captions over the cut, timed by forced alignment to what is actually said. Default libass-burn - the cheap tier, which ffmpeg burns in during the same pass, no browser. A cut with no speech in it is left alone whatever this says. Pass "off" to draw nothing: a music-only clip, footage that already carries subtitles, or a cut a project will caption itself. tiktok-pop, brand-block, clean-line and mini-doc are drawn by the browser: pick one when the look matters.

caption_script.description: What is said in the cut, when you know it: aligning against a known script beats transcribing. Omit to transcribe the clip itself. Needs captions.

caption_accent.description: Hex colour of the word being said in the captions - the karaoke highlight - and the cut's one accent: the pills' last word and the icon tiles wear it too. Match the brand; unset, the burned captions are plain white.

names.description: The brand, product and domain names, spelled the owner's way, comma-separated: "ShapelessAI, shapelessai.com". A recogniser hears "shapeless AI"; the captions must not misspell the customer. Always pass them when a take names the product.

caption_foreground.description: Hex colour of the burned captions' other words. White by default.

effects.description: Effects pinned to the person, one per line or semicolon: "<window> <lightning|sparks|glow> from <left|right|any> hand [index|palm|fingertips] [colour]", "<window> <kind> from face" or "<window> <kind> at x,y". The hand is found in every frame and the effect follows it, lightning shooting the way the finger points: @"watch this"+2 lightning from right hand; 4-6 sparks from any hand palm gold. left and right are the person's own hands; any is the safe pick. Colour: a hex or blue, purple, red, gold, green, white. The window must be where the hand is actually in view (look at the filmstrip); the result says how many frames it was found in. A strike lands with a sound when studio_sound or normalize_audio is on.

normalize_audio.description: Re-level the cut to broadcast loudness, keeping what was said, without the studio_sound cleaning. For a mix that was already produced.

plan.description: Resolve the whole call and render nothing: the paper edit comes back, every beat of the take kept or dropped, where each plays on the cut and what sits on it, with what an editor would send back (a bare beat, a picture that leaves before the thought ends or runs into the next one, the same picture twice). Plan with it until it reads right, then repeat the call without plan to render once.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: render_thumbnail
tools.title: Render a video thumbnail
tools.description: Package a finished video with its cover: one frame of it (frame_at, in seconds), three to five words, at most one picture. Filed beside the video as <video>-thumbnail.jpg, so a post that carries the video key gets the cover. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

video_key.description: The finished video (mediaKey from edit_footage or videoKey from render_video_project).

frame_at.description: Seconds into the video (or into frame_key) to take the face from.

frame_key.description: A clip to take the frame from instead, at its own resolution: the take behind the cut. frame_at then counts on it.

headline.description: Three to five words, not the title. *Stars* mark the accent words: "I hired *an AI*".

picture_key.description: One picture at most (an image media key): the product, the post, the number, the company's mark or the face of the person the video is about.

accent.description: Hex colour of the starred words. Defaults to the cut's accent.

foreground.description: Hex colour of the words. Default white.

outline.description: Hex colour of the contour and the scrim behind the words. Default near-black.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: demo_page
tools.title: Record a product demo
tools.description: A real browser opens a URL and performs the steps you name (type, click, hover, scroll, wait); returns an MP4 media key drawn like a screen-recorded demo, with a cursor and camera that follow each action. A page behind a login demos as its login wall. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

url.description: The absolute URL of the page to demo.

steps.description: One step per line or semicolon: "type acme.com into the URL field; click Analyze; wait 2; hover the first result; scroll to Pricing". Add "for 2s" to hold a step longer.

name.description: A 2-6 word filename for the clip, e.g. "analyze flow demo".

viewport.description: Which screen to demo on. mobile by default for a 9:16 clip (the page fills the reel), desktop otherwise or when the reel shows the desktop product.

aspect.description: The clip's shape. 9:16 by default so it fills a reel behind a cutout speaker.

zoom.description: Ease the camera onto each element touched. On by default; off shows the whole page.

browser_bar.description: Draw a browser bar with the address above the page. On by default.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: render_carousel
tools.title: Render a carousel
tools.description: Render your own HTML and CSS slides to a PDF (a LinkedIn document post) plus one PNG per slide (an Instagram carousel), each a media key. Slides are 1080x1350 unless you pass page; self-contained HTML only, no scripts or external URLs; src="media:<key>" places a library image. A render with clipped or unreadable text is refused with a per-element audit. SPENDS CREDIT: about $0.02 of engine cost a default call, billed with the plan's margin; budgetUsd caps it (default 2, max 10) and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

title.description: Short deck title (file naming and accessibility; render it yourself if you want it visible).

css.description: The deck's one shared stylesheet: palette, type scale, layout classes. Scope everything under .slide-canvas.

page.description: The canvas every slide is drawn on, in pixels. Default 1080x1350. Pick the shape the post will live in: 1080x1350 4:5 portrait (LinkedIn documents, Instagram portrait); 1080x1080 1:1 square; 1920x1080 16:9 landscape (slides, X, YouTube thumbnails). Anything between 480 and 2560px per side works; design your type scale for the canvas you chose, not for this default.

slides.description: 1-12 slides in order. Multi-slide: slide 1 is the hook read at thumbnail size; the last slide carries ONE call to action. Exactly 1 slide = a single-page infographic: the rendered PNG is the deliverable, designed to be fully read in-feed without a swipe.

headline.description: The slide's one-line essence (shown as a text preview while pixels render).

html.description: The slide's body markup — everything inside the fixed-size canvas. Static HTML only.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: speak
tools.title: Turn text into speech
tools.description: Read up to 2000 characters aloud into a WAV in the media library, in a preset voice (Sulafat, Charon, Kore, Achird, Erinome, Schedar) or a character's own voice id from characters_list, with an energy and a style line. Returns its media key. SPENDS CREDIT: about $0.03 of engine cost a default call, billed with the plan's margin; budgetUsd caps it (default 2, max 10) and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

text.description: What to say, exactly as it should be read. At most 2000 characters.

voice.description: A roster name or a character voice id. Default Charon.

energy.description: How the read moves: calm (measured and reassuring - explainers, anything serious or reflective); confident (the default: brisk, warm, matter-of-fact - product and brand video); energetic (bright and driving - launches, feature reveals, anything with momentum); hype (creator-loud - short-form hooks, reaction and meme-adjacent posts). Default confident.

style.description: Extra direction in plain words, e.g. "smile on the last line". Gemini voices only.

name.description: File name stem. Default: the voice name.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: caption_file
tools.title: Make a subtitle file
tools.description: Transcribe a video or audio file in the media library (up to 20 minutes) into a word-timed .srt or .vtt. Filed next to the source; the text also comes back inline. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

media_key.description: The video or audio in your library, e.g. from an upload.

names.description: Brand and product names to spell your way, comma-separated: "ShapelessAI, shapelessai.com".

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: plan_music
tools.title: Generate a music bed
tools.description: Generate an instrumental music bed from a style (genre, mood, instruments, tempo; never an artist) and get its media key with its beat grid (bpm, beat times), so a video can be cut on the beat. Pass the key as edit_footage's music. SPENDS CREDIT: about $0.06 of engine cost a default call, billed with the plan's margin; budgetUsd caps it (default 2, max 10) and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

style.description: Genre, mood, instrumentation and tempo - what the generator is given, near-verbatim.

duration_seconds.description: How long the video runs. The grid comes back covering that length, repeating as the bed loops - so a beat time is usable anywhere in the video, not just in the first loop.

allow_vocals.description: Lets the bed sing. Default false, because a voice under a narrator fights it - set it true when the track IS the post (a silent video, a music-led piece, a hook that wants a topline).

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: probe_media
tools.title: Inspect a video or audio file
tools.description: Look at a video or audio file in the media library: duration, size, frame rate, loudness, a filmstrip of timestamped frames, frames at chosen seconds, the waveform, and for speech every word with its time and the same words as numbered beats. Read it before edit_footage. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

media_key.description: The item to look at, as a mediaKey from media_library or any tool that returned one.

frames.description: Specific seconds to see, comma separated: "0, 4.5, 12". Up to 16. Omit for the filmstrip across the whole clip, which is usually what you want first.

frame_count.description: How many frames the filmstrip holds. 12 by default.

waveform.description: Also attach the audio as a waveform image with a second-ruler along it.

transcript.description: Time the words (on by default for anything with sound under eight minutes). false skips it - a music track, a clip you have already read.

names.description: The brand, product and domain names the transcript must spell the owner's way, comma-separated: "ShapelessAI, shapelessai.com".

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

annotations.title: Inspect a video or audio file

tools.name: find_photo
tools.title: Find a real photo
tools.description: Fetch one licensed real photograph (stock or Pixabay) or a blank meme template into the media library as a media key. Every result carries its licence; credit it when attributionRequired is true. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

query.description: What the photograph shows, concretely - subject, setting, mood.

source.description: Which library to search. "stock" by default.

orientation.description: Shape of the slot the photo fills. Portrait suits 9:16 video.

variant.description: Which of the results for this query, 0-based; wraps around what the source has. 0 (the default) is the largest match, and the same photo every time.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: find_footage
tools.title: Find stock footage
tools.description: Fetch one licensed real video clip (stock, Pixabay, the Internet Archive, NASA, Wikimedia Commons, reaction GIFs) into the media library as a media key. Search in two to four concrete words. B-roll only: no recognizable faces, logos or branded property. Free: budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) is held while it runs and released. Needs the write scope.

query.description: The subject on screen in two to four catalogue words - "rain window night", not a sentence describing the shot.

source.description: Which library to search. "stock" by default.

orientation.description: Shape of the slot the clip fills. Portrait (default) suits 9:16, and only "stock" can honour it - every other shelf returns what it has, so reframe those.

min_duration_seconds.description: Reject clips shorter than this. Leave unset unless a beat needs the length.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.

output.description: The tool's own result, shaped by the tool.

tools.name: find_face
tools.title: Find a person's photo
tools.description: Fetch a real photograph of a named person into the media library: their freely licensed Wikipedia portrait first, else the photo they publish themselves. Pass about (company or role) so a common name lands on the right person. Static use only; credit it when attributionRequired is true. Costs a fraction of a cent (about $0.007) from credit; budgetUsd (default 2, max 10) caps it and chargedUsd says what it cost. Needs the write scope.

person.description: The person's name as they spell it, e.g. 'Noah Shinn'.

about.description: Who they are, e.g. 'founder of Instinct'. Tells namesakes apart on the web.

variant.description: Which of their photos, 0-based; wraps around what exists.

budgetUsd.description: Optional: the most this call may spend, in dollars, default 2, max 10.
